And as you know, Ralph versus the city of Daytona Beach, the Supreme Court of Florida recognized that if a city, in this case, the city of Daytona Beach, assumed control over a beach area, then it had a duty to warn of dangers associated with the driving on the beach mixed with, and this is important, the lethal, as they said in their quote in the court, the lethal mixture of cars and sunbathers, people sunbathing on the beach. Now, there is a whole host of cases involving other accidents on the beach, people in traffic lanes, people drowning and surf, that we're not talking about. The Supreme Court again said, that's an actionable cause of action. So the trial judge, the original trial judge said, yes, this is a Ralph Butler case situation. Go forward. No, she was never asked that. And that is the exact danger that could have been prevented here had there been proper warning. I took the deposition. I'm sorry.
